input: Stainless steel vacuum-insulated water bottle with a screw cap, double-walled with a vacuum between the walls, 750 ml capacity, sold complete for consumer use.
note: The classic GRI 1 tension: Chapter 96 vacuum vessel versus Chapter 73 steel household article. Chapter 96's terms and the Section XV parts-of-general-use note decide it, so the case fails if the model reasons from material instead of reading the notes.

input: Portable laptop computer weighing 1.4 kg, containing a central processing unit, an integrated keyboard and a 14-inch display.
note: Named in the schedule almost verbatim, including the 10 kg weight test. Checks that an unambiguous eo nomine provision is reached without drifting into 8517 or a parts heading.

input: Lithium-ion traction battery pack used as the primary source of electrical power for a battery-electric passenger car.
note: Exercises GRI 6 at the statistical suffix: 8507.60.00 splits by end use, so getting the heading right and the suffix wrong is the expected failure mode. Scored separately as a rate-line match.

input: Men's short-sleeved T-shirt, 100% cotton jersey knit, crew neck, no pockets or trim, not underwear.
note: Textiles carry a deep statistical breakout keyed to garment category. Tests whether the model reads the sibling suffixes rather than stopping at the 8-digit line.

input: Household free-standing steel shelving unit for storage in a garage, powder-coated, assembled from bolted metal frames and shelves.
note: Also a Chapter 99 screening case: 9403.20.00 is enumerated in the Section 232 derivative aluminum notes, so the determination should raise that conditionally on origin.

input: Moulded polypropylene kitchen colander for draining pasta and washing vegetables, one piece with perforated bowl and two side handles, for household use.
note: A residual case by construction. 3924.10 breaks out dispensers, plates and bowls, and trays by name; a colander is none of them, so the correct answer is the 'Other' suffix. Retrieval is a bag-of-words search weighting a line's own description over its path, and a residual line's description is the single word 'Other' — so it can only be reached through the path, at lower weight. This case fails if the tool is pulled toward a named sibling because the sibling's words match the product's.

input: Cold-formed mild steel L-shaped mounting bracket, 80 mm by 80 mm, 3 mm thick, zinc-plated, with four pre-drilled bolt holes, used to fix machinery frames to a concrete floor. Not a fence post, ladder, pipe hanger or grounding rod.
note: The deepest residual basket in the schedule: 7326.90.86 itself is 'Other' and breaks out nine named articles before reaching '.88 Other'. The description rules the named siblings out explicitly, so the answer is determinate — but reaching it means walking past nine lines whose descriptions are more specific than the right one. The strongest single test of the eo nomine bias.

input: Household extension cord, 3 m of insulated copper conductor rated 125 V, moulded three-prong grounding plug on one end and a three-outlet socket block on the other.
note: The sibling to the residual: 8544.42.90 splits into '.10 Extension cords as defined in statistical note 7 to this chapter' and '.90 Other'. Getting this right requires reading a chapter statistical note to find out what the suffix means — the same class of instruction as the Chapter 91 reporting scheme, and the same failure if the tool answers from the line's wording alone.

input: Replacement glass inner liner for a vacuum flask, sold on its own as a spare part, silvered double-walled glass with the space between the walls evacuated. Supplied without any outer case or cap.
note: Deliberately paired with flask-1l: the same heading, the opposite side of the parts-versus-whole split. 9617 separates complete vessels from parts other than glass inners — and this good is a glass inner, which is the exclusion inside the parts line. A tool that pattern-matches 'vacuum flask' lands on the complete-vessel line that flask-1l tests, so the pair catches matching on the noun rather than reading the breakout.
